misconceptions.description: Treating a stapled set of artifacts as a capstone instead of one connected chain of judgment
misconceptions.trigger: artifacts appear in sequence with no decision linking one to the next
misconceptions.feedback: Show how each artifact follows from the value decision in the prior one, so the capstone reads as one argument.

misconceptions.description: Letting a later capstone artifact drop or contradict a value the earlier one committed to
misconceptions.trigger: implementation plan or memo violates the priority set in the tension map
misconceptions.feedback: Make later artifacts honor the value decisions earlier ones committed to, or revise the decision openly.

misconceptions.description: Delegating the integrative judgment to AI rather than using it to flag inconsistencies the teacher resolves
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts model edits that make artifacts agree without checking the underlying decision
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI to flag possible contradictions, then resolve each one yourself against your value decision.

misconceptions.description: Producing a uniformly confident, polished capstone that hides rather than reasons through hard tradeoffs
misconceptions.trigger: every artifact reaches a positive conclusion with no tension left visible
misconceptions.feedback: Surface at least one hard tradeoff and show how you reasoned through it; hidden tradeoffs are not judgment.
